questions.q: What specific hypothesis did the threat hunt team frame after Lesson 30's incident closed?
options: Whether Teresa Marsh's account had been compromised a second time
Whether WKSTN-FIN-14 needed to be isolated again
Whether the Sentinel analytics rule needed to be deleted
Whether the attacker used a different persistence technique against a second identity that wouldn't trigger impossible travel because its sign-in geography looked ordinary
questions.explain: The hypothesis deliberately targeted a different technique family and a sign-in pattern that wouldn't repeat Teresa's exact indicators.

questions.q: What MITRE ATT&CK technique did the hunting query target?
options: T1053.005 — Scheduled Task
T1486 — Data Encrypted for Impact
T1078 — Valid Accounts
T1114.003 — Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
questions.explain: The hunt queried OfficeActivity for inbox rules forwarding mail to external domains, which maps to MITRE ATT&CK T1114.003.

questions.q: Who did the hunt discover as a second, previously undetected compromised account?
options: A vendor account with excessive permissions
Daniel Oyelaran, a Compliance Operations Analyst, with an inbox rule forwarding wire/transfer-related mail to an external Gmail address
An IT administrator with a weak password
Teresa Marsh, found to be compromised a second time
questions.explain: Daniel's inbox rule, created nine days before Teresa's incident, silently forwarded financial mail to an external address.

questions.q: Why did Daniel Oyelaran's compromised account never trigger the impossible-travel analytics rule?
options: The sign-in that created the malicious inbox rule came from a residential IP in the same metro area he normally works from
The rule had been temporarily turned off that week
His account had MFA disabled, so no sign-in was logged at all
Impossible-travel rules don't apply to Compliance Operations accounts
questions.explain: Because the sign-in geography looked ordinary, it never produced the cross-location pattern the impossible-travel rule looks for.

questions.q: What did the hunt team do with their finding to prevent it from being a one-time discovery?
options: Documented it in a report and took no further technical action
Scheduled the hunting query as a new, entity-mapped Sentinel analytics rule tagged to the relevant MITRE ATT&CK technique
Disabled inbox rules entirely for every account in the tenant
Removed the OfficeActivity data source from Sentinel
questions.explain: Turning a hunt into a permanent, scheduled detection is what keeps the same gap from going uncaught again.
